name: Prashant Singh
specialty: I build the complex, data-heavy parts of SaaS products: dashboard builders, report builders, live maps and big data tables. In React and Next.js, with the backend when needed.
openTo: Full-time roles (remote, hybrid or on-site, happy to relocate) and freelance projects.
location: Kotdwara, India · Open to remote and relocation

summary.fullstack: Full-stack engineer with 4+ years of experience building the data-heavy parts of SaaS products: dashboard builders, report builders and live maps, from the React UI down to the API and database. At Unolo, a field-force management SaaS, I built the Custom Dashboards and GIS map modules. My own projects ship end to end on Next.js, Node.js, GraphQL, PostgreSQL and AWS.
summary.frontend: Frontend engineer with 4+ years of experience, specialising in complex, data-heavy interfaces: drag-and-drop dashboard builders, report builders and live maps that stay fast with large datasets. At Unolo, a field-force management SaaS, I built the Custom Dashboards and GIS map modules, and made the app load faster by lazy-loading heavy libraries. Strong in React, Next.js, TypeScript and GraphQL, and comfortable on the Node.js side when needed.

focus.title: Dashboard builders
focus.text: Drag-and-resize dashboards with charts, KPI cards and shared filters that save themselves as you work.

focus.title: Live maps
focus.text: Maps with live GPS, heatmaps and clustered markers that stay smooth with very large numbers of points.

focus.title: Reports & big tables
focus.text: Report builders, fast data tables and bulk Excel imports, so people can get answers out of their own data.

bullets: Built the **Custom Dashboards** module: users drag, resize, share and clone dashboards made of **7 chart types, 9 KPI types and map widgets**, with auto-save and shared filters (React Grid Layout, Highcharts, Apollo GraphQL).

Built the **GIS map engine** inside dashboards: point maps, heatmaps and clustered markers on Google Maps with Deck.gl. Used Supercluster so maps stay smooth with very large point sets, and cached reverse-geocoding to stop repeat Google Maps API calls.
Built the drag-and-drop **Custom Report builder** (React, TanStack Table, React Flow) with advanced filters, so customers can answer questions the standard reports can't.
Made the app **load faster** by splitting code, lazy-loading the heavy map and chart libraries, and trimming GraphQL queries.
Owned the frontend side of the **GraphQL contract** for dashboards and reports with the backend team.
Mentor junior developers on React architecture, reusable component patterns and Next.js SSR.
Built **live GPS tracking** screens with React and WebSockets, showing field staff moving on a map in real time.
Built **bulk Excel upload** flows so admins import large client and site lists in one go instead of adding them one by one.
Built shared TypeScript + Tailwind UI components reused across modules, keeping screens consistent.
Connected React and Redux screens to REST and GraphQL APIs, keeping live data in sync.
Made the web app work well on mobile screens with React, Redux and Tailwind CSS.
Ran AWS infrastructure (EC2, S3, Athena) and built Python tools to monitor usage and cut cloud costs.
Built automated reports and data-quality dashboards with Python, pandas and SQL.

projects.name: DSA Sheet
projects.oneLiner: Full-stack practice tracker: students work through DSA problems, tick them off and plan them on a calendar.
bullets: Designed for 10k–50k active users, and wrote the system design (HLD) and database schema (LLD) docs.
Cookie login with refresh tokens, and optimistic updates so ticks feel instant.
Deployed on AWS: CloudFront → EC2 → Nginx, serving Next.js and Express on one domain (no CORS).

projects.name: Career Glider
projects.oneLiner: Reads my Gmail, uses Claude AI to sort job-search emails by type, and shows them in a searchable dashboard.
bullets: GraphQL API that pulls Gmail with rate-limit handling and classifies each email with the Claude API.
Unit tests for the AI parser and Gmail throttling; typed error codes across the API.
